title: IIT JAM 2027 Physics (PH) — Full Length Mock Test 03
titleEn: IIT JAM 2027 Physics (PH) — Full Length Mock Test 03

questions.questionTextEn: A projectile is fired horizontally due north from a point in the Northern Hemisphere. Due to the Earth's rotation, the horizontal component of the Coriolis force deflects the projectile toward the
questions.explanationEn: The Coriolis force is $\vec{F}_C = -2m(\vec{\omega} \times \vec{v})$. In the Northern Hemisphere, $\vec{\omega}$ has an upward vertical component $\omega\sin\lambda\,\hat{k}$ (where $\lambda$ is latitude). For northward velocity $\vec{v} = v\hat{j}$, $\hat{k} \times \hat{j} = -\hat{i}$ (West), so $-\vec{\omega}\times\vec{v}$ points along $+\hat{i}$ (East), i.e., to the right of motion. Hence, option (B) is correct.

questions.questionTextEn: At a certain instant, a plane electromagnetic wave in vacuum has electric field $\vec{E}$ along $+\hat{y}$ and magnetic field $\vec{B}$ along $-\hat{x}$. The direction of energy flow (Poynting vector $\vec{S}$) is along
questions.explanationEn: The Poynting vector is $\vec{S} = \frac{1}{\mu_0}(\vec{E}\times\vec{B})$. Since $\hat{y} \times (-\hat{x}) = -(\hat{y}\times\hat{x}) = +\hat{z}$, energy propagates along $+\hat{z}$.

questions.questionTextEn: One mole of an ideal gas undergoes a free (Joule) expansion into vacuum, doubling its volume inside a thermally insulated rigid container. Which of the following is true for this process?
questions.explanationEn: In a free expansion into vacuum, $Q = 0$ and $W = 0$, so $\Delta U = 0$. For an ideal gas, $U = U(T)$, hence $\Delta T = 0$. Since entropy is a state function, $\Delta S = R \ln(V_f/V_i) = R \ln 2 > 0$. Hence, option (D) is correct.

questions.questionTextEn: The reciprocal lattice of a face-centered cubic (FCC) direct lattice with conventional lattice constant $a$ is a:
optionsEn: simple cubic lattice of lattice constant $\frac{2\pi}{a}$
face-centered cubic lattice of lattice constant $\frac{4\pi}{a}$
body-centered cubic lattice of lattice constant $\frac{2\pi}{a}$
body-centered cubic lattice of lattice constant $\frac{4\pi}{a}$
questions.explanationEn: The primitive vectors of an FCC lattice are $\vec{a}_1 = \frac{a}{2}(\hat{y}+\hat{z})$, $\vec{a}_2 = \frac{a}{2}(\hat{z}+\hat{x})$, $\vec{a}_3 = \frac{a}{2}(\hat{x}+\hat{y})$. Computing $\vec{b}_1 = 2\pi\frac{\vec{a}_2 \times \vec{a}_3}{\vec{a}_1 \cdot (\vec{a}_2 \times \vec{a}_3)}$ yields $\vec{b}_1 = \frac{2\pi}{a}(-\hat{x}+\hat{y}+\hat{z})$, and cyclic permutations for $\vec{b}_2, \vec{b}_3$. These are the primitive vectors of a BCC lattice with conventional cube edge $\frac{4\pi}{a}$. Hence, the correct option is (D).

questions.questionTextEn: A long solid cylindrical conductor of radius $R$ carries a steady current $I$ uniformly distributed across its cross-section. The ratio of the magnetic field magnitude at radial distance $r = R/2$ to that at $r = 2R$ is
questions.explanationEn: Inside ($r < R$), $B(r) = \frac{\mu_0 I r}{2\pi R^2}$, so $B(R/2) = \frac{\mu_0 I}{4\pi R}$. Outside ($r > R$), $B(r) = \frac{\mu_0 I}{2\pi r}$, so $B(2R) = \frac{\mu_0 I}{4\pi R}$. Their ratio is $1$.

questions.questionTextEn: For the standard Pauli matrices $\sigma_x = \begin{pmatrix} 0 & 1 \\ 1 & 0 \end{pmatrix}$, $\sigma_y = \begin{pmatrix} 0 & -i \\ i & 0 \end{pmatrix}$, and $\sigma_z = \begin{pmatrix} 1 & 0 \\ 0 & -1 \end{pmatrix}$, the commutator $[\sigma_x, \sigma_y] = \sigma_x\sigma_y - \sigma_y\sigma_x$ equals
questions.explanationEn: Direct multiplication gives $\sigma_x\sigma_y = \begin{pmatrix} i & 0 \\ 0 & -i \end{pmatrix} = i\sigma_z$ and $\sigma_y\sigma_x = -i\sigma_z$. Hence, $[\sigma_x, \sigma_y] = i\sigma_z - (-i\sigma_z) = 2i\sigma_z$. Hence, option (B) is correct.

questions.questionTextEn: In a radioactive decay chain $A \to B \to C$ where parent $A$ has a much longer half-life than daughter $B$ ($T_{1/2, A} \gg T_{1/2, B}$), secular equilibrium is established at $t \gg T_{1/2, B}$. In secular equilibrium, the ratio of the activities $\frac{A_B}{A_A} = \frac{\lambda_B N_B}{\lambda_A N_A}$ is:
questions.explanationEn: For $\lambda_A \ll \lambda_B$ and $\lambda_B t \gg 1$, $N_B(t) \approx \frac{\lambda_A}{\lambda_B} N_A(t)$, which implies $\lambda_B N_B \approx \lambda_A N_A$, so the activities of parent and daughter are equal ($A_B / A_A = 1$). Hence, option (B) is correct.

questions.questionTextEn: The eigenvalues of any non-zero skew-Hermitian matrix ($A^\dagger = -A$) are always
questions.explanationEn: If $A\vec{v} = \lambda\vec{v}$ ($\vec{v} \neq \vec{0}$), then $\vec{v}^\dagger A \vec{v} = \lambda \|\vec{v}\|^2$. Taking the conjugate transpose and using $A^\dagger = -A$ gives $-\vec{v}^\dagger A \vec{v} = \lambda^* \|\vec{v}\|^2$, so $\lambda^* = -\lambda$. Thus every eigenvalue has zero real part, meaning it is purely imaginary or zero. Hence, option (D) is correct.

questions.questionTextEn: A rigid body of radius of gyration $k_G$ about its center of mass oscillates as a physical pendulum in a vertical plane. The time period of small oscillations is minimum when the distance $l$ between the pivot and the center of mass equals
questions.explanationEn: The period is $T = 2\pi\sqrt{\frac{k_G^2 + l^2}{gl}} = 2\pi\sqrt{\frac{1}{g}\left(l + \frac{k_G^2}{l}\right)}$. Differentiating $l + k_G^2/l$ with respect to $l$ gives $1 - k_G^2/l^2 = 0 \implies l = k_G$.

questions.questionTextEn: For a particle of mass $m$ in a symmetric one-dimensional finite square potential well ($V(x) = -V_0 < 0$ for $|x| < a$, $V(x) = 0$ for $|x| > a$), how many bound states exist as $V_0 \to 0^+$?
questions.explanationEn: In 1D, any symmetric attractive potential well of arbitrarily small depth $V_0 > 0$ always supports at least one bound state (specifically, the nodeless even-parity ground state). As $V_0 \to 0^+$, exactly one bound state persists. Hence, option (D) is correct.

questions.questionTextEn: A particle of mass $m$ moves in a one-dimensional potential $V(x) = \frac{a}{x^2} - \frac{b}{x}$ for $x > 0$, where $a$ and $b$ are positive constants. The angular frequency of small oscillations about its stable equilibrium position is
questions.explanationEn: Setting $V'(x) = -\frac{2a}{x^3} + \frac{b}{x^2} = 0$ gives the equilibrium position $x_0 = \frac{2a}{b}$. The effective stiffness is $k_{\text{eff}} = V''(x_0) = \frac{6a}{x_0^4} - \frac{2b}{x_0^3} = \frac{6a b^4}{16 a^4} - \frac{2b^4}{8a^3} = \frac{b^4}{8a^3}$. Hence $\omega = \sqrt{\frac{k_{\text{eff}}}{m}} = \sqrt{\frac{b^4}{8ma^3}}$.

questions.questionTextEn: In a Colpitts oscillator, the resonant tank circuit consists of an inductor $L$ in parallel with two series capacitors $C_1$ and $C_2$. The frequency of oscillation $f_0$ is:
questions.explanationEn: In a Colpitts tank circuit, the two capacitors $C_1$ and $C_2$ are effectively in series across the inductor $L$, giving an equivalent capacitance $C_{\text{eq}} = \frac{C_1 C_2}{C_1 + C_2}$. Thus the oscillation frequency is $f_0 = \frac{1}{2\pi\sqrt{L C_{\text{eq}}}} = \frac{1}{2\pi}\sqrt{\frac{C_1 + C_2}{L C_1 C_2}}$. Hence, the correct option is (D).

questions.questionTextEn: In one-dimensional quantum mechanics, the commutator $[\hat{x}, \hat{p}_x^3]$ equals:
questions.explanationEn: Using the identity $[\hat{x}, f(\hat{p}_x)] = i\hbar f'(\hat{p}_x)$ (easily verified by repeated product rule), we get $[\hat{x}, \hat{p}_x^3] = 3i\hbar\hat{p}_x^2$. Hence, option (C) is correct.

questions.questionTextEn: Consider a classical ultra-relativistic ideal gas of $N$ non-interacting particles in $3$ dimensions with single-particle dispersion $\epsilon = cp$. The adiabatic index $\gamma = C_P / C_V$ of this gas is:
questions.explanationEn: By the generalized equipartition theorem, each linear degree of freedom ($\epsilon \propto |p|$) in 3D contributes $k_B T$ rather than $\frac{1}{2}k_B T$ (explicitly, $Z_1 \propto V \int_0^\infty p^2 e^{-\beta cp}\,dp \propto V T^3$, so $U = -\frac{\partial \ln Z}{\partial \beta} = 3Nk_B T$ and $P = \frac{Nk_B T}{V}$). Thus $C_V = 3Nk_B$, $C_P = 4Nk_B$, and $\gamma = \frac{4}{3}$. Hence, option (A) is correct.

questions.questionTextEn: A relativistic proton of rest mass $m_p$ strikes a stationary proton to produce a proton-antiproton pair via $p + p \to p + p + p + \bar{p}$. The minimum (threshold) kinetic energy of the incident proton in the laboratory frame is:
questions.explanationEn: Equating the Lorentz invariant $s = E^2 - p^2 c^2$ in the lab and CM frames at threshold (where all four final particles are at rest in the CM frame): $(E_{\text{lab}} + m_p c^2)^2 - p_{\text{lab}}^2 c^2 = (4m_p c^2)^2 \implies 2m_p^2 c^4 + 2E_{\text{lab}} m_p c^2 = 16m_p^2 c^4 \implies E_{\text{lab}} = 7m_p c^2$. Therefore, the threshold kinetic energy is $K_{\text{th}} = E_{\text{lab}} - m_p c^2 = 6m_p c^2$. Hence, option (B) is correct.

questions.questionTextEn: A block of mass $m$ moving with speed $v$ on a frictionless surface collides and sticks to a stationary block of mass $2m$. The fraction of the initial kinetic energy dissipated in this completely inelastic collision is
questions.explanationEn: By momentum conservation, the final common speed is $v_f = \frac{mv}{m + 2m} = \frac{v}{3}$. The final kinetic energy is $K_f = \frac{1}{2}(3m)\left(\frac{v}{3}\right)^2 = \frac{1}{3}K_i$. Therefore, the fraction dissipated is $\frac{K_i - K_f}{K_i} = 1 - \frac{1}{3} = \frac{2}{3}$. Hence, option (C) is correct.

questions.questionTextEn: A gas mixture consists of $2\text{ moles}$ of an ideal monatomic gas and $3\text{ moles}$ of an ideal rigid diatomic gas. The effective adiabatic index $\gamma_{\text{mix}} = C_P / C_V$ of the mixture is:
questions.explanationEn: The molar heat capacity at constant volume of the mixture is $C_{V,\text{mix}} = \frac{n_1 C_{V1} + n_2 C_{V2}}{n_1 + n_2} = \frac{2(\frac{3}{2}R) + 3(\frac{5}{2}R)}{5} = \frac{21}{10}R$. Thus $C_{P,\text{mix}} = C_{V,\text{mix}} + R = \frac{31}{10}R$, giving $\gamma_{\text{mix}} = \frac{31}{21}$. Hence, option (D) is correct.

questions.questionTextEn: The value of the improper integral $\int_0^\infty x^3 e^{-2x}\,dx$ is
questions.explanationEn: Substituting $u = 2x$ ($dx = du/2$) gives $\int_0^\infty \left(\frac{u}{2}\right)^3 e^{-u}\frac{du}{2} = \frac{1}{16}\int_0^\infty u^3 e^{-u}\,du = \frac{\Gamma(4)}{16} = \frac{3!}{16} = \frac{6}{16} = \frac{3}{8}$. Hence, option (A) is correct.

questions.questionTextEn: A damped harmonic oscillator of mass $m$, damping coefficient $b$, and spring constant $k$ is driven by a harmonic force $F_0\cos(\omega t)$. The maximum time-averaged power absorbed from the driving agent (occurring at $\omega = \sqrt{k/m}$) is
questions.explanationEn: The time-averaged power is $\langle P \rangle = \frac{1}{2} F_0 v_0 \cos\phi$. At velocity resonance ($\omega = \omega_0$), velocity is in phase with the driving force ($\cos\phi = 1$) and $v_0 = \frac{F_0}{b}$. Thus $\langle P \rangle_{\max} = \frac{1}{2}F_0\left(\frac{F_0}{b}\right) = \frac{F_0^2}{2b}$.

questions.questionTextEn: Positronium is a bound state of an electron and a positron (same mass $m_e$, opposite charges). Compared to a hydrogen atom with an infinitely heavy proton (Bohr radius $a_0$, ground-state energy $-13.6\text{ eV}$), the ground-state energy and interparticle separation of positronium in the Bohr model are:
questions.explanationEn: The reduced mass of positronium is $\mu = \frac{m_e \cdot m_e}{m_e + m_e} = \frac{m_e}{2}$. Since $E_1 \propto \mu$ and $r_1 \propto \mu^{-1}$, positronium has ground-state energy $\frac{-13.6}{2} = -6.8\text{ eV}$ and Bohr radius $2a_0$. Hence, option (A) is correct.

questions.questionTextEn: Two thin lenses made of the same glass (same dispersive power) with focal lengths $f_1$ and $f_2$ are separated by a distance $d$ in air. The combination is free from longitudinal chromatic aberration when $d$ equals
questions.explanationEn: From $\frac{1}{F} = \frac{1}{f_1} + \frac{1}{f_2} - \frac{d}{f_1 f_2}$, setting $\delta\left(\frac{1}{F}\right) = 0$ with $\frac{\delta f_1}{f_1} = \frac{\delta f_2}{f_2} = -\omega_d$ (same glass) yields $-\frac{\delta f_1}{f_1^2} - \frac{\delta f_2}{f_2^2} + d\left(\frac{\delta f_1}{f_1^2 f_2} + \frac{\delta f_2}{f_1 f_2^2}\right) = 0 \implies \frac{1}{f_1} + \frac{1}{f_2} = \frac{2d}{f_1 f_2} \implies d = \frac{f_1 + f_2}{2}$.

questions.questionTextEn: A solid sphere of radius $R$ has a radially varying volume charge density $\rho(r) = k r$, where $k$ is a positive constant and $r$ is the distance from the center. The magnitude of the electric field inside the sphere ($r < R$) is
questions.explanationEn: The enclosed charge within radius $r$ is $q_{\text{enc}} = \int_0^r (k r')(4\pi r'^2\,dr') = \pi k r^4$. By Gauss's law, $E(4\pi r^2) = \frac{\pi k r^4}{\varepsilon_0} \implies E(r) = \frac{k r^2}{4\varepsilon_0}$.

questions.questionTextEn: A uniform thin rod of length $L$ is pivoted about a horizontal axis perpendicular to the rod at a distance $d$ from its center of mass to form a physical pendulum. The value of $d$ that minimizes its small-oscillation time period is
questions.explanationEn: The period is $T = 2\pi\sqrt{\frac{k^2 + d^2}{gd}}$, where $k = \sqrt{\frac{I_{\text{cm}}}{M}} = \frac{L}{\sqrt{12}} = \frac{L}{2\sqrt{3}}$ is the radius of gyration. Minimizing $\frac{k^2}{d} + d$ with respect to $d$ yields $d = k = \frac{L}{2\sqrt{3}}$. Hence, option (B) is correct.

questions.questionTextEn: In a single-stage RC-coupled common-emitter BJT amplifier, the voltage gain falls off at low frequencies and at high frequencies primarily due to, respectively:
optionsEn: inter-electrode junction capacitances at low frequencies, and coupling/bypass capacitors at high frequencies
emitter resistor $R_E$ at low frequencies, and collector resistor $R_C$ at high frequencies
stray wiring inductance at low frequencies, and thermal noise at high frequencies
coupling and emitter bypass capacitors at low frequencies, and transistor junction/stray capacitances at high frequencies
questions.explanationEn: At low frequencies, the reactance $X_C = \frac{1}{2\pi f C}$ of the series coupling capacitors and emitter bypass capacitor becomes large, attenuating the signal and reducing the gain. At high frequencies, these large capacitors act as short circuits, while the small internal $p$-$n$ junction capacitances ($C_{be}$, Miller-multiplied $C_{bc}$) and stray capacitances shunt the signal to ground, causing the high-frequency roll-off. Hence, the correct option is (D).

questions.questionTextEn: A thin conducting wire bent into a square loop of side length $a$ carries a steady current $I$. The magnitude of the magnetic field at the geometric center of the square is
questions.explanationEn: Each of the $4$ sides lies at perpendicular distance $d = a/2$ from the center and subtends $\theta_1 = \theta_2 = 45^\circ$. Using $B_{\text{side}} = \frac{\mu_0 I}{4\pi d}(\sin 45^\circ + \sin 45^\circ) = \frac{\mu_0 I}{2\pi a}\sqrt{2}$, multiplying by $4$ gives $B = \frac{2\sqrt{2}\,\mu_0 I}{\pi a}$.

questions.questionTextEn: In an Ohm's law experiment, independent measurements yield voltage $V = (100 \pm 3)\text{ V}$ and current $I = (10.0 \pm 0.4)\text{ A}$. Using standard root-sum-square (quadrature) error propagation for independent uncertainties, the resistance $R = V/I$ is
questions.explanationEn: The nominal resistance is $R = \frac{100}{10.0} = 10.0\ \Omega$. The relative uncertainties are $\frac{\sigma_V}{V} = \frac{3}{100} = 0.03$ and $\frac{\sigma_I}{I} = \frac{0.4}{10.0} = 0.04$. Adding independent fractional errors in quadrature gives $\frac{\sigma_R}{R} = \sqrt{(0.03)^2 + (0.04)^2} = 0.05$, so $\sigma_R = 0.05 \times 10.0 = 0.5\ \Omega$. Hence, option (B) is correct.

questions.questionTextEn: Two blocks of masses $m$ and $2m$ are connected by a massless spring of spring constant $k$ on a frictionless horizontal table. The angular frequency of small longitudinal oscillations of the system is
questions.explanationEn: The reduced mass of the two-body system is $\mu = \frac{m(2m)}{m + 2m} = \frac{2}{3}m$. Therefore, the angular frequency of relative oscillation is $\omega = \sqrt{\frac{k}{\mu}} = \sqrt{\frac{3k}{2m}}$. Hence, option (B) is correct.

questions.questionTextEn: In an $\text{NaCl}$ crystal (FCC lattice with $\text{Na}^+$ at $(0,0,0)$ and $\text{Cl}^-$ at $(\frac{1}{2}, \frac{1}{2}, \frac{1}{2})$), let $f_{\text{Na}}$ and $f_{\text{Cl}}$ be the atomic form factors of $\text{Na}^+$ and $\text{Cl}^-$, respectively. The geometrical structure factor $S_{hkl}$ for the $(111)$ and $(200)$ reflections are, respectively:
questions.explanationEn: The structure factor of $\text{NaCl}$ is $S_{hkl} = S_{\text{FCC}} \cdot [f_{\text{Na}} + f_{\text{Cl}} e^{i\pi(h+k+l)}]$. For all-odd or all-even indices, $S_{\text{FCC}} = 4$. For $(111)$, $h+k+l = 3$ (odd), so $e^{i3\pi} = -1$ and $S_{111} = 4(f_{\text{Na}} - f_{\text{Cl}})$. For $(200)$, $h+k+l = 2$ (even), so $e^{i2\pi} = +1$ and $S_{200} = 4(f_{\text{Na}} + f_{\text{Cl}})$. Hence, the correct option is (B).

questions.questionTextEn: A parallel-plate capacitor with circular plates of radius $R$ is charged by a steady current $I$. Neglecting fringing fields, the ratio of the magnetic field magnitude at radial distance $r = R/2$ from the axis between the plates to that at $r = 2R$ outside the plates is
questions.explanationEn: Between the plates ($r < R$), the enclosed displacement current is $I_d(r) = I\frac{r^2}{R^2}$, giving $B(r) = \frac{\mu_0 I r}{2\pi R^2}$, so $B(R/2) = \frac{\mu_0 I}{4\pi R}$. Outside ($r > R$), $I_d = I$, so $B(2R) = \frac{\mu_0 I}{2\pi(2R)} = \frac{\mu_0 I}{4\pi R}$. Their ratio is $1$.

questions.questionTextEn: Let $C$ be the closed triangular path in the $xy$-plane with vertices $(0, 0)$, $(2, 0)$, and $(2, 2)$, traversed counterclockwise. The value of the line integral $\oint_C (y^2\,dx + 3xy\,dy)$ is
questions.explanationEn: By Green's theorem, $\oint_C (P\,dx + Q\,dy) = \iint_D \left(\frac{\partial Q}{\partial x} - \frac{\partial P}{\partial y}\right)dx\,dy$ with $P = y^2$ and $Q = 3xy$. Then $\frac{\partial Q}{\partial x} - \frac{\partial P}{\partial y} = 3y - 2y = y$. Over the triangle $0 \le x \le 2$, $0 \le y \le x$: $\int_0^2 \int_0^x y\,dy\,dx = \int_0^2 \frac{x^2}{2}\,dx = \left[\frac{x^3}{6}\right]_0^2 = \frac{4}{3}$. Hence, option (A) is correct.

questions.questionTextEn: Consider a particle of mass $m$ in a symmetric 1D infinite square well $V(x) = 0$ for $-a < x < a$ and $V(x) = \infty$ for $|x| \ge a$. Which of the following statement(s) is/are TRUE?
optionsEn: The ground-state energy is $E_1 = \frac{\pi^2 \hbar^2}{8 m a^2}$
The ground-state wavefunction has even parity ($\psi_1(-x) = \psi_1(x)$)
The first excited state wavefunction vanishes at $x = 0$
The energy spacing $E_{n+1} - E_n$ is independent of $n$
questions.explanationEn: The total width of the well is $L = 2a$, so $E_n = \frac{n^2 \pi^2 \hbar^2}{2m(2a)^2} = \frac{n^2 \pi^2 \hbar^2}{8ma^2}$, giving $E_1 = \frac{\pi^2 \hbar^2}{8ma^2}$ (A True). Since $V(-x) = V(x)$, eigenstates alternate in parity: $n = 1$ is $\cos(\pi x/(2a))$ (even, B True) and $n = 2$ is $\sin(\pi x/a)$ (odd, vanishes at $x = 0$, C True). $E_{n+1} - E_n = (2n + 1)E_1$ increases linearly with $n$ (D False). Hence, (A), (B), and (C) are correct.

questions.questionTextEn: For a dilute ideal gas of hard-sphere molecules of mass $m$ and diameter $d$ at pressure $P$ and temperature $T$, which of the following scaling relations is/are CORRECT?
optionsEn: At constant pressure $P$, the mean free path $\lambda \propto T$
At constant temperature $T$, the mean free path $\lambda \propto P^{-1}$
At constant number density $n$, the mean free path $\lambda$ is independent of $T$
At constant pressure $P$, the collision frequency $z \propto T^{1/2}$
questions.explanationEn: Using $\lambda = \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}\pi d^2 n} = \frac{k_B T}{\sqrt{2}\pi d^2 P}$: (A) True at fixed $P$, $\lambda \propto T$; (B) True at fixed $T$, $\lambda \propto P^{-1}$; (C) True at fixed $n$, $\lambda$ is independent of $T$. For collision frequency $z = \bar{v}/\lambda$: at fixed $P$, $\bar{v} \propto T^{1/2}$ and $\lambda \propto T$, so $z \propto T^{-1/2}$ (D False). Hence, (A), (B), and (C) are correct.

questions.questionTextEn: Let $u = u(x, y)$ and $v = v(x, y)$ be smooth functions with Jacobian $J = \frac{\partial(u, v)}{\partial(x, y)}$. Which of the following statement(s) is/are true?
optionsEn: For $u = x + y$ and $v = x^2 + 2xy + y^2$, the Jacobian $J$ is identically zero
For $u = x + y$ and $v = x - y$, the Jacobian $J$ equals $2$
If $u$ and $v$ are functionally dependent ($F(u, v) = 0$ identically), then $J = 0$
If $J \neq 0$ at a point, then $\frac{\partial(x, y)}{\partial(u, v)} = \frac{1}{J}$ locally
questions.explanationEn: (C) True: Functional dependence implies linearly dependent gradients, so $J = 0$. (D) True: By the inverse function theorem, $J_{\text{inv}} = J^{-1}$. (A) True: Here $v = u^2$, so $J = \begin{vmatrix} 1 & 1 \\ 2(x+y) & 2(x+y) \end{vmatrix} = 0$. (B) False: $\begin{vmatrix} 1 & 1 \\ 1 & -1 \end{vmatrix} = -2 \neq 2$. Hence, options (A), (C), and (D) are correct.

questions.questionTextEn: A particle moves in a plane along a curve described in polar coordinates $(r(t), \theta(t))$. Which of the following statement(s) is/are ALWAYS correct?
optionsEn: The radial component of acceleration is $\ddot{r} - r\dot{\theta}^2$
If the transverse acceleration is identically zero, then $r^2\dot{\theta}$ is constant in time
The transverse (azimuthal) component of acceleration is $r\ddot{\theta} + 2\dot{r}\dot{\theta}$
If $\dot{r} = 0$, the radial acceleration must be zero
questions.explanationEn: (A) and (C) are the exact polar acceleration components. (B) Note that $r\ddot{\theta} + 2\dot{r}\dot{\theta} = \frac{1}{r}\frac{d}{dt}(r^2\dot{\theta})$, so $a_\theta = 0 \implies r^2\dot{\theta} = \text{const}$ (Kepler's second law). (D) False: For uniform circular motion ($\dot{r} = 0, \ddot{r} = 0$), $a_r = -r\dot{\theta}^2 \neq 0$. Hence, options (A), (B), and (C) are correct.

questions.questionTextEn: In a standard shunt Zener diode voltage regulator with fixed input voltage $V_s > V_Z$, fixed series resistor $R_s$, and variable load resistor $R_L$ (assuming the Zener remains in breakdown), which of the following statement(s) is/are correct?
optionsEn: The total current drawn from the source $I_s = \frac{V_s - V_Z}{R_s}$ remains constant as $R_L$ varies
The Zener current $I_Z$ is maximum when the load is open-circuited ($R_L \to \infty$)
Decreasing $R_L$ increases the load current $I_L$ and decreases the Zener current $I_Z$
The power dissipated in the Zener diode increases as $R_L$ decreases
questions.explanationEn: While the Zener is in breakdown, the output node is clamped at $V_Z$. (A) $I_s = \frac{V_s - V_Z}{R_s}$ is independent of $R_L$ (True). (B) Since $I_Z = I_s - I_L = I_s - \frac{V_Z}{R_L}$, $I_Z$ is maximum when $I_L = 0$ ($R_L \to \infty$) (True). (C) Decreasing $R_L$ raises $I_L = V_Z / R_L$, so $I_Z = I_s - I_L$ decreases (True). (D) Power in the Zener $P_Z = V_Z I_Z$ *decreases* as $R_L$ decreases (False). Hence, options (A), (B), and (C) are correct.

questions.questionTextEn: Light of wavelength $\lambda = 300\text{ nm}$ is incident on a metallic surface with work function $\phi = 2.14\text{ eV}$. Taking $hc = 1242\text{ eV}\cdot\text{nm}$, which of the following statement(s) is/are TRUE?
optionsEn: The energy of each incident photon is $4.14\text{ eV}$
The maximum kinetic energy of emitted photoelectrons is $2.00\text{ eV}$
The threshold wavelength of the metal is approximately $580\text{ nm}$
questions.explanationEn: Photon energy $E = \frac{1242}{300} = 4.14\text{ eV}$ (A True). $K_{\max} = E - \phi = 4.14 - 2.14 = 2.00\text{ eV}$ (B True), so stopping potential $V_0 = K_{\max}/e = 2.00\text{ V}$ (C True). Threshold wavelength $\lambda_0 = \frac{1242}{2.14} \approx 580.4\text{ nm}$ (D True). Hence, (A), (B), (C), and (D) are all correct.

questions.questionTextEn: A thin parallel-sided film of uniform thickness $t$ and refractive index $n$ is suspended in air and illuminated by monochromatic light of wavelength $\lambda$ at angle of incidence $i$ (refracted angle $r$). Which of the following statements is/are correct?
optionsEn: Constructive interference in reflected light occurs when $2nt\cos r = \left(m + \frac{1}{2}\right)\lambda$ for $m = 0, 1, 2, \dots$
As the film becomes extremely thin ($t \ll \lambda$), the film appears dark in reflected light
The reflected and transmitted interference patterns are complementary (where reflection is maximum, transmission is minimum)
Increasing the angle of incidence $i$ increases the optical path difference $2nt\cos r$
questions.explanationEn: By energy conservation (for a non-absorbing film), $R + T = 1$, so reflected and transmitted patterns are complementary (True). As $t \to 0$, the $\pi$ reflection phase shift at the front face yields destructive interference (dark in reflection, True), and bright reflection requires $2nt\cos r = (m + 1/2)\lambda$ (True). Increasing $i$ increases $r$ and decreases $\cos r$, thus decreasing $2nt\cos r$ (False).

questions.questionTextEn: For any three vectors $\vec{A}, \vec{B}, \vec{C} \in \mathbb{R}^3$, which of the following identities is/are ALWAYS valid?
questions.explanationEn: (C) True: Standard BAC-CAB vector triple product identity. (B) True: The Jacobi identity follows immediately by summing the three cyclic permutations of the BAC-CAB rule. (D) True: Cyclic invariance of the scalar triple product. (A) False: The cross product is not associative in general. Hence, options (B), (C), and (D) are correct.

questions.questionTextEn: Consider a magnetic vector potential $\vec{A}(\vec{r})$ related to the magnetic field by $\vec{B} = \nabla \times \vec{A}$. Which of the following statements is/are correct?
optionsEn: The vector potential $\vec{A}$ is uniquely determined by $\vec{B}$ without specifying any gauge condition
The magnetic flux through an open surface $S$ bounded by a closed curve $C$ equals $\oint_C \vec{A}\cdot d\vec{l}$
For a uniform magnetic field $\vec{B} = B_0\hat{z}$, $\vec{A} = \frac{1}{2}(\vec{B}\times\vec{r}) = \frac{B_0}{2}(-y\hat{x} + x\hat{y})$ is a valid vector potential
Adding the gradient of any smooth scalar function $\nabla\Lambda(\vec{r})$ to $\vec{A}$ leaves $\vec{B}$ unchanged

questions.questionTextEn: An electric field in a region is given by $\vec{E} = (3x\hat{i} + 4y\hat{j} + 5z\hat{k})\text{ V/m}$. The net outward electric flux through the closed surface of a cube of side $1\text{ m}$ occupying $0 \le x, y, z \le 1$ is ______ $\text{V}\cdot\text{m}$. (Answer in integer)
questions.explanationEn: By the divergence theorem, $\Phi_E = \iiint (\nabla\cdot\vec{E})\,dV = (3 + 4 + 5) \times 1^3 = 12\text{ V}\cdot\text{m}$.

questions.questionTextEn: A uniaxial birefringent crystal has $|n_e - n_o| = 0.008$ at wavelength $\lambda = 640\text{ nm}$. The minimum thickness of a quarter-wave plate made from this crystal is ______ $\mu\text{m}$. (Answer in integer)
questions.explanationEn: The minimum thickness for a quarter-wave plate is $d = \frac{\lambda}{4|n_e - n_o|} = \frac{640 \times 10^{-9}}{4 \times 0.008} = 2.0 \times 10^{-5}\text{ m} = 20\ \mu\text{m}$.

questions.questionTextEn: A series $RC$ circuit consists of a $250\text{ k}\Omega$ resistor and a $40\ \mu\text{F}$ capacitor. The time constant of the circuit is ______ $\text{s}$. (Answer in integer)
questions.explanationEn: The $RC$ time constant is $\tau = RC = (250 \times 10^3)(40 \times 10^{-6}) = 10\text{ s}$.

questions.questionTextEn: A particle of mass $2\text{ kg}$ moves in a central force field with a constant angular momentum of $40\text{ kg}\cdot\text{m}^2/\text{s}$ about the force center. The areal velocity $\frac{dA}{dt}$ swept out by its position vector, in $\text{m}^2/\text{s}$, is ____. (Answer in integer)
questions.explanationEn: The areal velocity is $\frac{dA}{dt} = \frac{L}{2m} = \frac{40}{2 \times 2} = 10\text{ m}^2/\text{s}$.

questions.questionTextEn: A beam of particles with energy $E = \frac{9}{5}V_0$ is incident on a 1D potential step of height $V_0$. The transmission coefficient $T$ across the step is ______ (Round off to 2 decimal places).
The line integral $\oint_C (-y\,dx + x\,dy)$ evaluated counterclockwise along the ellipse $\frac{x^2}{9} + \frac{y^2}{4} = 1$ is equal to $k\pi$. The value of $k$ is ____. (Answer in integer)
questions.explanationEn: By Green's theorem, $\oint_C (-y\,dx + x\,dy) = \iint_D (1 - (-1))\,dx\,dy = 2\,\text{Area}(D)$. For an ellipse with semi-axes $a = 3$ and $b = 2$, $\text{Area}(D) = \pi ab = 6\pi$, so the integral equals $12\pi$, giving $k = 12$.

questions.questionTextEn: For the matrix $A = \begin{pmatrix} 1 & 3 \\ 2 & 4 \end{pmatrix}$, the trace of $A^2$ is ____. (Answer in integer)
questions.explanationEn: Computing $A^2 = \begin{pmatrix} 1 & 3 \\ 2 & 4 \end{pmatrix}\begin{pmatrix} 1 & 3 \\ 2 & 4 \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} 7 & 15 \\ 10 & 22 \end{pmatrix}$, we obtain $\text{Tr}(A^2) = 7 + 22 = 29$.

questions.questionTextEn: The temperature of a blackbody radiation cavity of fixed volume is doubled from $300\text{ K}$ to $600\text{ K}$. The ratio of the final entropy of the photon gas to its initial entropy is ______ (Answer in integer).
questions.explanationEn: For a photon gas in a cavity of volume $V$, $S = \frac{4}{3}a V T^3 \propto T^3$. Doubling $T$ increases the entropy by a factor of $2^3 = 8$.

questions.questionTextEn: The mass defect of a ${}^4_2\text{He}$ nucleus is $0.03038\text{ u}$. Taking $1\text{ u} = 931.5\text{ MeV}/c^2$, the binding energy per nucleon of ${}^4_2\text{He}$ is ______ $\text{MeV}$ (Round off to 2 decimal places).
questions.explanationEn: Total binding energy is $B = 0.03038 \times 931.5 = 28.299\text{ MeV}$. Dividing by $A = 4$ gives $B/A = 7.075\text{ MeV} \approx 7.07\text{ MeV}$.

questions.questionTextEn: The minimum number of $2$-input NAND gates required to construct a $2$-input XOR gate (with only uncomplemented inputs $A$ and $B$ available) is ______. (Answer in integer)
questions.explanationEn: A $2$-input XOR gate can be realized using exactly $4$ two-input NAND gates: $G_1 = \overline{AB}$, $G_2 = \overline{A \cdot G_1}$, $G_3 = \overline{B \cdot G_1}$, and $Y = \overline{G_2 \cdot G_3} = A\bar{B} + \bar{A}B = A \oplus B$. Thus, the minimum number is $4$.

questions.questionTextEn: The periodic triangular wave $f(x) = |x|$ for $-2 < x < 2$ (with period $T = 4$) is expanded in a Fourier series $f(x) = \frac{a_0}{2} + \sum_{n=1}^{\infty} a_n \cos\left(\frac{n\pi x}{2}\right)$. The value of the coefficient $a_1$ is ____. (Rounded off to two decimal places)
questions.explanationEn: With half-period $L = 2$, $a_1 = \frac{2}{L}\int_0^L x\cos\left(\frac{\pi x}{2}\right)dx = \int_0^2 x\cos\left(\frac{\pi x}{2}\right)dx = \left[\frac{2x}{\pi}\sin\frac{\pi x}{2} + \frac{4}{\pi^2}\cos\frac{\pi x}{2}\right]_0^2 = \frac{4}{\pi^2}(-1 - 1) = -\frac{8}{\pi^2} \approx -0.81$.

questions.questionTextEn: A charged $20\ \mu\text{F}$ capacitor is discharged through a $50\text{ k}\Omega$ resistor starting at $t = 0$. The time elapsed until the electrostatic energy stored in the capacitor drops to $25\%$ of its initial value is ______ $\text{s}$. (Round off to 3 decimal places)
questions.explanationEn: The time constant is $\tau = RC = (50 \times 10^3)(20 \times 10^{-6}) = 1.0\text{ s}$. Since $U(t) = U_0 e^{-2t/\tau}$, setting $e^{-2t/\tau} = \frac{1}{4}$ gives $\frac{2t}{\tau} = \ln 4 = 2\ln 2 \implies t = \tau\ln 2 \approx 0.693\text{ s}$.

questions.questionTextEn: The mirror nuclei ${}^{15}_7\text{N}$ and ${}^{15}_8\text{O}$ differ in binding energy by $\Delta B = 3.54\text{ MeV}$. Attributing this entire difference to the Coulomb term $-a_c \frac{Z(Z - 1)}{A^{1/3}}$ in the semi-empirical mass formula, the Coulomb constant $a_c$ is ______ $\text{MeV}$ (Round off to 2 decimal places).
questions.explanationEn: The Coulomb energy difference is $\Delta B = \frac{a_c}{A^{1/3}}[8(7) - 7(6)] = \frac{14 a_c}{15^{1/3}}$. Solving for $a_c$ gives $a_c = \frac{3.54 \times 15^{1/3}}{14} = \frac{3.54 \times 2.4662}{14} \approx 0.62\text{ MeV}$.

questions.questionTextEn: A neutral pion ($\pi^0$, rest mass $135\text{ MeV}/c^2$) moving with kinetic energy $135\text{ MeV}$ decays in flight into two photons emitted collinearly along its direction of motion. The energy of the forward-moving (higher-energy) photon is ______ $\text{MeV}$ (Round off to 1 decimal place).
questions.explanationEn: The pion's total energy is $E = 135 + 135 = 270\text{ MeV}$ ($\gamma = 2$, $\beta = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$), and its momentum is $pc = \sqrt{270^2 - 135^2} = 135\sqrt{3}\text{ MeV}$. For collinear decay ($E_1 + E_2 = E$ and $E_1 - E_2 = pc$), the forward photon energy is $E_1 = \frac{E + pc}{2} = \frac{270 + 135\sqrt{3}}{2} \approx 251.9\text{ MeV}$.

questions.questionTextEn: An NPN silicon BJT ($\beta = 99$, $V_{BE} = 0.7\text{ V}$) is biased using a voltage-divider network with $V_{CC} = 12\text{ V}$, $R_1 = 30\text{ k}\Omega$ (from $V_{CC}$ to base), $R_2 = 10\text{ k}\Omega$ (from base to ground), $R_C = 2.5\text{ k}\Omega$, and $R_E = 1.0\text{ k}\Omega$. Using exact Thevenin analysis, the collector-to-emitter voltage $V_{CE}$ is ______ $\text{V}$. (Rounded off to two decimal places)
questions.explanationEn: The Thevenin equivalent at the base is $V_{\text{th}} = 12 \times \frac{10}{30 + 10} = 3.0\text{ V}$ and $R_{\text{th}} = \frac{30 \times 10}{30 + 10} = 7.5\text{ k}\Omega$. By KVL in the base-emitter loop: $I_B = \frac{V_{\text{th}} - V_{BE}}{R_{\text{th}} + (\beta + 1)R_E} = \frac{3.0 - 0.7}{7.5 + 100(1.0)} = \frac{2.3}{107.5}\text{ mA} \approx 0.02140\text{ mA}$. Thus $I_C = 99 I_B \approx 2.118\text{ mA}$ and $I_E = 100 I_B \approx 2.140\text{ mA}$. Finally, $V_{CE} = V_{CC} - I_C R_C - I_E R_E = 12 - (2.118)(2.5) - (2.140)(1.0) \approx 4.57\text{ V}$.

questions.questionTextEn: A series $RLC$ resonant circuit has resistance $R = 10\ \Omega$, inductance $L = 50\text{ mH}$, and capacitance $C = 2\ \mu\text{F}$. The full width at half maximum (bandwidth $\Delta f$, in $\text{Hz}$) of its average power resonance curve is ______ $\text{Hz}$. (Round off to 2 decimal places)
questions.explanationEn: The angular-frequency bandwidth is $\Delta\omega = \frac{R}{L} = \frac{10}{0.05} = 200\text{ rad/s}$. Converting to cyclic frequency gives $\Delta f = \frac{\Delta\omega}{2\pi} = \frac{100}{\pi} \approx 31.83\text{ Hz}$.

questions.questionTextEn: A solid sphere of radius $R = 2\text{ m}$ centered at the origin has a radially varying mass density $\rho(r) = \frac{3r}{4\pi}\text{ kg/m}^3$. The total mass of the sphere, in $\text{kg}$, is ____. (Answer in integer)
questions.explanationEn: Integrating in spherical coordinates: $M = \int_0^2 \rho(r)\,4\pi r^2\,dr = \int_0^2 \left(\frac{3r}{4\pi}\right)(4\pi r^2)\,dr = 3\int_0^2 r^3\,dr = 3\left[\frac{r^4}{4}\right]_0^2 = 3(4) = 12\text{ kg}$.

questions.questionTextEn: A small steel sphere of radius $1\text{ mm}$ and density $7800\text{ kg/m}^3$ falls vertically through a viscous oil of density $800\text{ kg/m}^3$ and viscosity $0.7\text{ Pa}\cdot\text{s}$. Taking $g = 9.8\text{ m/s}^2$, the terminal velocity of the sphere, in $\text{cm/s}$, is ____. (Rounded off to two decimal places)
questions.explanationEn: By Stokes' law, $v_t = \frac{2(\rho_s - \rho_l)g r^2}{9\eta} = \frac{2(7800 - 800)(9.8)(10^{-3})^2}{9 \times 0.7} = \frac{0.1372}{6.3} \approx 0.02178\text{ m/s} \approx 2.18\text{ cm/s}$.

questions.questionTextEn: Two identical metal blocks, each of constant heat capacity $400\text{ J/K}$, are initially at $900\text{ K}$ and $400\text{ K}$. They serve as the hot and cold reservoirs for a reversible heat engine until they reach a common temperature. The maximum work that can be extracted is ______ $\text{kJ}$ (Answer in integer).
questions.explanationEn: For zero total entropy change, $T_f = \sqrt{T_1 T_2} = \sqrt{900 \times 400} = 600\text{ K}$. The maximum work is $W_{\max} = C(T_1 + T_2 - 2T_f) = 400(900 + 400 - 1200) = 40{,}000\text{ J} = 40\text{ kJ}$.

questions.questionTextEn: A thin convex lens of focal length $+10\text{ cm}$ and a thin concave lens of focal length $-15\text{ cm}$ are placed coaxially $25\text{ cm}$ apart. A point object is placed $15\text{ cm}$ to the left of the convex lens. The distance of the final real image to the right of the concave lens is ______ $\text{cm}$. (Round off to 1 decimal place)
questions.explanationEn: For the convex lens ($u_1 = -15\text{ cm}$, $f_1 = +10\text{ cm}$): $\frac{1}{v_1} = \frac{1}{10} - \frac{1}{15} = \frac{1}{30} \implies v_1 = +30\text{ cm}$. This forms a virtual object at $u_2 = 30 - 25 = +5\text{ cm}$ for the concave lens ($f_2 = -15\text{ cm}$). Thus $\frac{1}{v_2} = -\frac{1}{15} + \frac{1}{5} = \frac{2}{15} \implies v_2 = +7.5\text{ cm}$ to the right of the concave lens.
